newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower after options expiry.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower after options expiry.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Friday, on moderate volumes, ahead of the expiry of April gold, silver and platinum options at the close.

"The market only closed lower on some last minute selling from a couple of parties, after a featureless day with the options expiry producing little new direction," Credit Lyonnais Rouse chief bullion dealer, Scott Mehlman, said.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.50 at $352.90 an ounce, after trading a $355.50-352.50 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 25,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $352.00/352.50, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $352.80 and the New York close Thursday around $353.10/60.
Spot gold prices have drifted in a $350-355 range this week, after a month-long recovery from three year lows around $336, driven by funds covering near-record short positions.
In data released Friday, COMEX gold open interest fell a further 3,825 lots Thursday to 169,484 contracts, the lowest level since September last year.

Implied lease rates for gold fell to their lowest level in months also Friday, with the one month rate down to 0.77 percent, suggesting there was little interest in renewed shorting of the market, analysts said.
Physical gold demand in the first quarter 1997 was running at the highest levels since 1993, New York based World Gold Council analyst, George Milling-Stanley said.
Gold imports by Dubai, an entrepot center for gold distribution to India, the world's largest consuming country, rose to a record 46 tonnes in January 1997, from 24 tonnes last year, he said.

Other analysts noted that demand was rising, particularly in Asia, after gold prices fell to three year lows early this year, in a pattern similar to the jump in demand in the 1987-1989 period when gold prices fell from a peak of over $500 an ounce.
"With demand for gold still quite strong at around the $350 level, gold prices could continue higher over the next few trading days, challenging resistance at $360," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.

Gold prices also received some support this week from sharply lower US stock and bond prices, but some concern remains about the potential for further European central bank gold sales after the introduction of European Monetary Union approaches, analysts said.
Last week the Swiss government announced a plan to sell 40 tonnes of gold a year over ten years to fund a Holocaust victims fund.

COMEX May silver ended down 3.0 cents at $5.285 an ounce, after trading a 5.345-5.270 range, but May silver is having trouble holding above $5.300, after breaking out of a year-long downtrend back in February, traders said.
NYMEX April platinum ended down $2.20 at $384.00 an ounce, after trading a $388.50-383.50 range, while NYMEX June palladium closed down $1.60 at $157.00 an ounce.

But most analysts still see Russian exports of platinum group metals falling in 1997, with Russian palladium stockpiles down to less than one year's supply, and mine production at the Norilsk plant threatened by industrial action.
